| f-2b01 | defect | MINOR | MINOR — object-literal and class-expression members get two DIFFERENT wrong answers, and neither is covered by a test. The value-shape rule keys on variable_declarator and public_field_definition, so for the extremely common TS module idiom `export const api = { get() {}, post() {}, put: () =&gt; {} }`: (a) `get` and `post` are emitted, but the unclassified variable_declarator is spliced through, so they land at FILE scope as `p.ts::get` / `p.ts::post` with the `api` segment lost — two modules each exporting `get` collide on one address; and (b) `put: () =&gt; {}` is an object `pair`, not a binding node, so it produces NO element at all — a real exported callable is invisible to search. The same split hits `const C = class { m() {} }`, which yields a file-scope `p.ts::m` and no element for C. This is consistent with the documented splice rule ('declarations attach to the nearest named ancestor'), so it is not a contract violation — but it is unfixtured, so a future change to either behaviour is silent. | crates/parsers/src/source.rs:20-28 (FUNCTION_BINDINGS/FUNCTION_VALUES), :93-101, :38-50 (splice); crates/parsers/fixtures/sample.ts | [x] checked | Smallest fix, and it is deliberately small: add these two shapes to sample.ts and lock TODAY'S behaviour in the golden, so the gap is recorded rather than accidental. Actually changing the behaviour (scoping members under the binding, and teaching the rule about `pair` — which also needs a `key` entry in NAME_FIELDS) is a follow-up packet, not this one; no acceptance criterion promises object-literal members. | — | — | [acceptance-criteria](../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria), [architecture](../../impl-guide.dd.md#architecture) | MEASURED by me at the reviewed sha. `export const api = { get() {}, post() {}, put: () =&gt; {} };` =&gt; file typescript p.ts #0 1-5 / function method_definition p.ts::get #0 2-2 / function method_definition p.ts::post #1 3-3 — no `api` element, no `put` element, both method addresses at file depth. `const C = class { m() {} };` =&gt; function method_definition p.ts::m #0 2-2 only. |

| f-2b03 | question | NIT | NIT — anonymous default exports produce no element for the exported thing. `export default function () {}` yields an empty forest, and `export default class { m() {} }` yields only a file-scope `p.ts::m`. This is the documented and correct nameless-declaration behaviour ('Nameless declarations are skipped; their children are not'), and I am NOT calling it a defect — but TypeScript makes the anonymous default export a routine idiom in a way Rust and Python never do, so the rule costs materially more here than where it was designed. Worth a conscious decision (synthesise a name from the module basename, or accept the hole) rather than inheriting it by default. | crates/parsers/src/source.rs:56-60 (node_name gate); docs/services/scanner.md (Key decisions — nameless declarations) | [x] checked | — | — | — | [non-goals](../../plan.dd.md#non-goals) | MEASURED by me: `export default function () {}` =&gt; single row `file typescript p.ts #0 1-1`. `export default class { m() {} }` =&gt; `function method_definition p.ts::m #0 2-2` and no container row. |
